concerns.text: The mixed‑effects model is fit on only nine observations (3 datasets × 3 methods). This sample size is far too small to reliably estimate fixed effects, random intercept variance, and to assess model assumptions, leading to severely underpowered statistical inference.

ARI and NMI are logit‑transformed to create `logit_fidelity`, but the plan does not specify how values of 0 or 1 (which make the logit undefined) will be handled, risking runtime errors or biased transformations.

It is unclear whether the mixed‑effects model uses ARI, NMI, or a combined metric as the response (`logit_fidelity`). Mixing two distinct fidelity measures without justification threatens construct validity.

Potential confounds such as total cell count, gene count, and number of highly variable genes are not included as covariates, yet they can influence both geometric descriptors and clustering fidelity, leaving residual confounding unaddressed.
